target_fields.permit_id: The permit application number assigned at filing.
target_fields.permit_type: The numeric permit type code 1-8 from the code table.
target_fields.status: The current status word of the permit.
target_fields.filed_date: The date the permit application was filed.
target_fields.issued_date: The date the permit was issued.
target_fields.completed_date: The date the work was signed off as complete; blank while not complete.
target_fields.street_number: The street number of the work site.
target_fields.street_name: The street name of the work site followed by its suffix abbreviation.
target_fields.zipcode: The five-digit ZIP code of the work site.
target_fields.estimated_cost: The cost estimated on the application, in whole US dollars.
target_fields.revised_cost: The cost as revised after plan review, in whole US dollars.
target_fields.existing_stories: Number of storeys of the building before the work.
target_fields.proposed_stories: Number of storeys of the building after the work.
target_fields.existing_use: The current use of the building.
target_fields.proposed_use: The use of the building after the work.
target_fields.description: Free-text description of the permitted work.

transforms.identity: The column already holds the field in target format.
transforms.date_mdy: A month/day/year text date converted to YYYY-MM-DD.
transforms.date_dmy: A day/month/year text date converted to YYYY-MM-DD.
transforms.date_yyyymmdd: An 8-digit YYYYMMDD date converted to YYYY-MM-DD.
transforms.cents_to_dollars: An amount in cents divided by 100.
transforms.thousands_to_dollars: An amount in thousands of dollars multiplied by 1000.
transforms.decode_codelist: A partner letter code translated through the source's code list to a type name and then to its numeric code.
transforms.type_name_to_code: A permit type name translated to its numeric code with the code table.
transforms.address_number: The street number taken from a combined site-address column.
transforms.address_street: The street name and suffix taken from a combined site-address column.

pair_col_desc: Milestone date; see the note below the table.
date_pair_note: Columns {a} and {b} hold the {f1} and the {f2}, but which is which was not documented.
errata_swap: The descriptions of {a} and {b} were exchanged by mistake; each column holds what is described under the other.
errata_unit: Since release {release}, column {col} is exported in {unit}, whatever its description says.
errata_rename: Column {old} is now named {new} in the export file; its description is unchanged.
schema_header: Target schema. Every source must be mapped to all target fields below. Dates are YYYY-MM-DD and amounts are whole US dollars. The permit type code table and the transform menu follow.
intro: {agency} receives building-permit exports from partners. There are {n} sources, {first} to {last}; each has its own column names, a data dictionary and sample rows. For every source and every target field, find the column that holds the field (or null) and the transform from the menu. Dictionaries can carry notes and errata that override the table; columns may be renamed, mislabelled, or look like a target field without being one; some questions (which date is which, day/month order) are settled only by the values. Each source is graded separately and counts only if all its fields are right.
answer_line: Your final answer is one JSON object mapping each source id to an object with every target field as a key and either null or [column, transform], for example {example}.

tools.read_target_schema: Show the target fields, the permit type code table and the transform menu.
tools.list_sources: List sources (id | partner | columns | rows), paged with offset and limit.
tools.read_dictionary: Show one source's data dictionary with its notes and errata.
tools.read_rows: Show CSV rows of one source with its export header (offset, limit up to 15).
tools.column_profile: Profile one column of one source: blanks, distinct values, min, max and examples.

unit_prompt: Map source {src} to the target schema using read_target_schema, read_dictionary, read_rows and column_profile, applying its notes and errata. End with exactly one final line: UNIT | {src2} | <JSON object mapping every target field to null or [column, transform]>
